tasks.task_name: Document core team structure and organization
tasks.description:
Define and document the core project team structure consisting of 4-5 people as specified in the requirement specification. This includes establishing the organizational hierarchy with Product Manager (1), Technical Lead (1), Backend/CLI Developers (2), and Quality Assurance (1).

The team structure must be formally documented to ensure clarity in roles, reporting lines, and team composition. This foundational task enables proper resource allocation and clear accountability across the project.

Reference requirement: '6.1 Core Team Structure' which defines a Project Team of 4-5 people with specific role allocations.
tasks.task_notes: This is a foundational task that must be completed early as it defines the team composition. Consider creating a visual organizational chart and a written document that can be shared with stakeholders.

requirement_snippets:
Project Team (4-5 people)
├── Product Manager (1)
├── Technical Lead (1)
├── Backend/CLI Developer (2)
└── Quality Assurance (1)
success_criteria: Team structure document clearly shows 4-5 person composition
All five roles are defined with headcount allocation
Organizational hierarchy is visually represented

tasks.task_name: Define Product Manager role responsibilities and scope
tasks.description:
Establish comprehensive Product Manager role definition including all responsibilities and expectations as outlined in section 6.2.1 of the requirement specification.

The Product Manager role encompasses: defining and prioritizing the feature roadmap, gathering user requirements and feedback, coordinating between stakeholders and the development team, managing project timeline and milestones, ensuring business requirements are met, and creating user documentation and marketing materials.

This role definition serves as the foundation for hiring, onboarding, and performance evaluation of the Product Manager. It ensures clear expectations and accountability for product-related deliverables.

Reference requirement: '6.2.1 Product Manager' responsibilities section.

key_responsibilities: Coordinate between stakeholders and development team

tasks.task_notes: This role definition should be detailed enough to use for hiring and onboarding. Consider adding skills and qualifications needed for success in this role.

requirement_snippets:
Product Manager
**Responsibilities:**
- Define and prioritize feature roadmap
- Gather user requirements and feedback
- Coordinate between stakeholders and development team
- Manage project timeline and milestones
- Ensure business requirements are met
- User documentation and marketing materials
success_criteria: All six responsibility areas are documented
Role scope includes feature roadmap management
Role scope includes stakeholder coordination
Role scope includes business requirement validation
Documentation and marketing materials are assigned to this role
dependencies: Document core team structure and organization

tasks.task_name: Create Product Manager MVP deliverables framework
tasks.description:
Implement the Product Manager MVP deliverables as specified in section 6.2.1, which includes four critical deliverables: user stories and acceptance criteria, MVP scope definition, user testing plan, and go-to-market strategy for the CLI tool.

These deliverables form the product management baseline for the MVP phase. They ensure that product requirements are clearly defined, scope is controlled, quality is validated through user testing, and market readiness is achieved.

Each deliverable must be created as a concrete artifact that can be used by the development team and stakeholders. The user stories should include acceptance criteria, the MVP scope should define clear boundaries, the testing plan should outline validation approach, and the go-to-market strategy should detail launch approach for the CLI tool.

Reference requirement: '6.2.1 Product Manager - MVP Deliverables' section.
tasks.task_notes: These deliverables are interdependent. User stories inform scope definition, which in turn influences the testing plan and go-to-market strategy. Consider creating templates or frameworks for each deliverable type.

requirement_snippets:
**MVP Deliverables:**
- User stories and acceptance criteria
- MVP scope definition
- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool
success_criteria: User stories document with acceptance criteria is created
MVP scope definition document is created
User testing plan document is created
Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool is created
All four deliverables are complete and approved

This role definition serves as the foundation for hiring, onboarding, and performance evaluation of the Technical Lead. It ensures clear technical leadership, architectural consistency, and quality standards across the codebase. The Technical Lead is responsible for both hands-on implementation and team mentorship.

Reference requirement: '6.2.2 Technical Lead' responsibilities section.
tasks.task_notes: This role is critical as it bridges technical execution and team leadership. The Technical Lead must have both strong technical skills and mentoring capabilities. Note the specific mention of Notion API integration as a key responsibility.

tasks.task_name: Recruit and onboard project team members
tasks.description:
Execute the recruitment and onboarding process to build the complete project team as defined in the core team structure. This involves hiring 4-5 people total: 1 Product Manager, 1 Technical Lead, 2 Backend/CLI Developers, and 1 Quality Assurance engineer.

This task translates the defined team structure into an operational team by conducting hiring processes, selecting candidates that match the role requirements, and onboarding them with the appropriate role documentation and expectations.

The team composition specified in the requirements must be met to ensure adequate capacity and skill coverage for the CLI tool project, particularly given the emphasis on Notion API integration and quality assurance.

Reference requirement: '6.1 Core Team Structure' which specifies the exact team composition required.
tasks.task_notes: This task depends on having clear role definitions in place. The team size range of 4-5 people suggests some flexibility, likely in whether to hire 1 or 2 Backend/CLI Developers initially. Consider hiring critical roles (Technical Lead, Product Manager) first, then expanding the team.

tasks.task_name: Develop user stories with acceptance criteria for MVP

User stories must capture user requirements and translate them into actionable development tasks. Each user story should follow best practices (As a... I want... So that...) and include specific, testable acceptance criteria that define when the story is complete.

This deliverable directly enables the development team to understand user needs and build the right features. It also provides the Quality Assurance team with clear validation criteria.

Reference requirement: '6.2.1 Product Manager - MVP Deliverables: User stories and acceptance criteria'.

parameters.format: structured user story format with acceptance criteria

tasks.task_notes: User stories are foundational for all development work. They should be prioritized and sized appropriately for MVP scope. Consider using a standard format and tool (e.g., Jira, Linear) for tracking. This deliverable directly feeds into sprint planning and development.

- MVP scope definition
- User testing plan

tasks.task_name: Define MVP scope boundaries and feature set
tasks.description:
Create a comprehensive MVP scope definition document that clearly defines what is included and excluded from the minimum viable product for the CLI tool project. This is a critical Product Manager deliverable as specified in section 6.2.1.

The MVP scope definition must establish clear boundaries to prevent scope creep and ensure the team focuses on essential features that deliver core value. It should list included features, explicitly call out deferred features, and provide rationale for scope decisions.

This document serves as the north star for the development team and helps manage stakeholder expectations. It directly supports the Product Manager's responsibility to ensure business requirements are met while delivering a viable product quickly.

Reference requirement: '6.2.1 Product Manager - MVP Deliverables: MVP scope definition'.

parameters.format: structured document with in-scope and out-of-scope sections

tasks.task_notes: This is a high-priority deliverable as it gates all development work. The scope definition should be aligned with user stories but may precede detailed story writing. Consider using a MoSCoW (Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have) framework for clarity.

requirement_snippets:
**MVP Deliverables:**

- MVP scope definition
- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool

tasks.task_name: Create comprehensive user testing plan for MVP
tasks.description:
Develop a detailed user testing plan that defines how the CLI tool will be validated with real users during the MVP phase. This is a critical Product Manager deliverable as specified in section 6.2.1.

The user testing plan must specify: testing objectives, target user segments, testing methodology (e.g., usability testing, beta testing), success metrics, timeline, and feedback collection mechanisms. It should align with the Product Manager's responsibility to gather user requirements and feedback.

This plan ensures that the CLI tool meets actual user needs before broader release. It provides a structured approach to validation and creates a feedback loop for product improvement.

Reference requirement: '6.2.1 Product Manager - MVP Deliverables: User testing plan'.
tasks.task_notes: The testing plan should be realistic given the team size and MVP timeline. Consider phased testing (internal alpha, limited beta, broader beta). Coordinate with the Quality Assurance role for technical testing aspects. This plan focuses on user validation, not technical QA.

requirement_snippets:

- MVP scope definition
- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool

tasks.task_name: Develop go-to-market strategy for CLI tool launch

Create a comprehensive go-to-market (GTM) strategy specifically for the CLI tool launch. This is a critical Product Manager deliverable as specified in section 6.2.1.

The GTM strategy must define: target audience and personas, value proposition and positioning, distribution channels, launch timeline and phases, marketing and communication plan, documentation and support approach, and success metrics for launch.

This strategy ensures coordinated and effective launch of the CLI tool to the market. It connects the Product Manager's responsibilities for user documentation, marketing materials, and ensuring business requirements are met. The strategy should account for the technical nature of CLI tool users and appropriate developer marketing channels.

Reference requirement: '6.2.1 Product Manager - MVP Deliverables: Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool'.
tasks.task_notes: The GTM strategy for a CLI tool differs from traditional software launches. The implementation must handle: Notion API authentication and token management, API request/response handling, rate limiting and retry logic, error handling for API failures, data transformation between Notion and CLI formats, and API version compatibility.

Given the explicit mention of Notion API integration in the Technical Lead responsibilities, this is a high-priority technical implementation that requires careful design and robust error handling. The integration must be reliable, performant, and maintainable.

tasks.task_notes: This is a critical integration task. Notion API has specific rate limits and authentication requirements that must be handled properly. Consider using official Notion SDK if available, or implement robust HTTP client with proper error handling. This integration will be used by multiple CLI commands, so it must be well-abstracted.
